components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 他把书包放在椅子边上。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ shūbāo fàng zài yǐzi biānshàng.
example.english: He put his backpack beside the chair.
example.fact: Earth's magnetic north pole is not fixed at one spot but drifts constantly, having moved over 600 kilometers since 1900. It is currently migrating from northern Canada toward Siberia at roughly 50 kilometers per year, driven by changes deep in Earth's molten outer core.

examples.hanzi: 商店就在银行的边上。
examples.pinyin: Shāngdiàn jiù zài yínháng de biānshang.
examples.english: The shop is right next to the bank.

examples.hanzi: 孩子坐在妈妈边上看书。
examples.pinyin: Háizi zuò zài māma biānshang kàn shū.
examples.english: The child sits beside Mom reading.

components.note: 立 (stand) — a person standing on the ground line. As a radical it appears in 站 stand, 位 seat, 竟; also in 建立 establish.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 谈判双方在这个问题上的立场完全不同。
example.pinyin: tánpàn shuāngfāng zài zhège wèntí shàng de lìchǎng wánquán bùtóng.
example.english: The two sides in the negotiation have completely different positions on this issue.
example.fact: The 1978 Camp David Accords succeeded partly because U.S. mediators kept Egypt and Israel's negotiating teams in separate cabins for much of the thirteen days, preventing face-to-face clashes over entrenched positions and letting written proposals shuttle back and forth instead. The technique, sometimes called "single-text negotiation," is still taught in diplomatic training today.

examples.hanzi: 请站在我的立场想一想。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhàn zài wǒ de lìchǎng xiǎng yi xiǎng.
examples.english: Please think about it from my standpoint.

examples.hanzi: 他的立场很坚定，不会轻易改变。
examples.pinyin: Tā de lìchǎng hěn jiāndìng, bú huì qīngyì gǎibiàn.
examples.english: His position is firm and won't change easily.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
心 (heart) — feelings and will: 想, 思, 感; 志 is what the heart is set on, ambition.
士 (shì) is only a loose sound hint for zhì.

example.hanzi: 她凭着坚强的意志完成了马拉松比赛。
example.pinyin: tā píngzhe jiānqiáng de yìzhì wánchéngle mǎlāsōng bǐsài.
example.english: She finished the marathon through sheer willpower.
example.fact: The Comrades Marathon in South Africa, first run in 1921, covers roughly 90 kilometers between Durban and Pietermaritzburg and has a strict twelve-hour cutoff enforced by officials who physically pull exhausted runners off the course the instant the finish-line gun fires. Finishers within the cutoff earn a bronze, silver, or gold medal depending on their time, but anyone even a second late receives nothing.

examples.hanzi: 他是个意志很坚强的人，从不轻易放弃。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè yìzhì hěn jiānqiáng de rén, cóng bù qīngyì fàngqì.
examples.english: He is a strong-willed person who never gives up easily.

examples.hanzi: 这次失败没有打败他的意志。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shībài méiyǒu dǎbài tā de yìzhì.
examples.english: This failure did not break his will.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person 亻 beside two 二: kindness is how people treat each other. 仁 rén also sounds like 人 rén.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart, as in 想, 爱, 念; 慈 is a loving, kind heart.
兹 (zī) — near sound — 慈 is cí; 兹 also sounds out 磁 cí.

example.hanzi: 国王以仁慈著称,从不轻易处死囚犯。
example.pinyin: guówáng yǐ réncí zhùchēng, cóng bù qīngyì chǔsǐ qiúfàn.
example.english: The king was known for his benevolence and rarely executed prisoners.
example.fact: Emperor Ashoka of ancient India, after a brutal conquest of Kalinga around 261 BC, reportedly renounced further warfare and had edicts carved on pillars across his empire promoting nonviolence, animal welfare, and care for the sick. Several of these Ashokan pillars, including the one at Sarnath topped by four lions, still stand today, and the lion capital was later adopted as modern India's national emblem.

examples.hanzi: 老奶奶对每个人都很仁慈。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo nǎinai duì měi gè rén dōu hěn réncí.
examples.english: The old lady is kind to everyone.

examples.hanzi: 法官对第一次犯错的年轻人比较仁慈。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān duì dì-yī cì fàncuò de niánqīngrén bǐjiào réncí.
examples.english: The judge was fairly lenient toward the young man who erred for the first time.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.

example.hanzi: 他的手表是爷爷留给他的传家宝。
example.pinyin: tā de shǒubiǎo shì yéye liú gěi tā de chuánjiābǎo.
example.english: His wristwatch is a family heirloom left to him by his grandfather.
example.fact: Wristwatches only became standard for men after World War I; before that they were considered mainly a woman's accessory, while men carried pocket watches. Soldiers in the trenches found pocket watches impractical to check under fire, so many strapped them to their wrists with leather cuffs, a battlefield workaround that permanently shifted men's fashion once the soldiers came home.

examples.hanzi: 我的手表慢了五分钟。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒubiǎo màn le wǔ fēnzhōng.
examples.english: My watch is five minutes slow.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈给我买了一块新手表。
examples.pinyin: Māma gěi wǒ mǎi le yí kuài xīn shǒubiǎo.
examples.english: Mom bought me a new watch.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water: 河, 深, 浅; 测 was measuring the depth of water.
则 (zé) is close to cè; same part in 侧 cè and 厕 cè.

example.hanzi: 医生给我测了一下血压。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi wǒ cè le yíxià xuèyā.
example.english: The doctor measured my blood pressure.
example.fact: 测 comes from gauging water depth and now forms 测量 (measure), 测试 (test), 预测 (predict), 猜测 (guess) and 测验 (quiz). In a lab or hospital, 测 + thing is the standard verb: 测体温, 测血压.

examples.hanzi: 明天有一场汉语测验。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān yǒu yì chǎng Hànyǔ cèyàn.
examples.english: There's a Chinese test tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 你能猜测一下结果吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng cāicè yíxià jiéguǒ ma?
examples.english: Can you guess the result?

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks mounds and earth, as in 院, 阶, 防; 隧 is a passage dug through a hill.
遂 (suì) gives the sound exactly: 隧 suì.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 这条隧道穿过阿尔卑斯山,连接了两个国家。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo suìdào chuānguò ā'ěrbēisī shān, liánjiēle liǎng gè guójiā.
example.english: This tunnel passes through the Alps, connecting two countries.
example.fact: The Gotthard Base Tunnel in Switzerland, opened in 2016, runs 57 kilometers through the Alps and is the world's longest railway tunnel — engineers had to bore through rock reaching 45°C and account for the mountain settling by several centimeters as material was removed. It cut the Zurich-to-Milan rail journey by roughly an hour.

examples.hanzi: 火车穿过隧道后，眼前出现了大海。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē chuānguò suìdào hòu, yǎnqián chūxiàn le dàhǎi.
examples.english: After the train passed through the tunnel, the sea appeared in front of us.

examples.hanzi: 隧道里的灯光很暗，开车要小心。
examples.pinyin: Suìdào lǐ de dēngguāng hěn àn, kāichē yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: The lights in the tunnel are dim, so drive carefully.

components.note: 王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.

example.hanzi: 这座博物馆展示了从古代到现代的艺术发展。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò bówùguǎn zhǎnshìle cóng gǔdài dào xiàndài de yìshù fāzhǎn.
example.english: This museum shows the development of art from ancient times to the modern era.
example.fact: The Bauhaus school, founded in Weimar, Germany in 1919, fused fine art with industrial craft and pioneered much of what is now called modern design — clean geometric forms, exposed materials, and furniture meant for mass production rather than individual commission. The Nazi government forced it to close in 1933, but its exiled teachers, including Walter Gropius and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, carried its ideas into American architecture schools.

examples.hanzi: 现代人的生活节奏越来越快。
examples.pinyin: Xiàndài rén de shēnghuó jiézòu yuèláiyuè kuài.
examples.english: The pace of life of modern people is getting faster and faster.

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢现代艺术，不太喜欢传统绘画。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan xiàndài yìshù, bú tài xǐhuan chuántǒng huìhuà.
examples.english: She likes modern art and doesn't care much for traditional painting.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — traditional 導 had 道 (road) plus 寸 (hand): a hand leading along a road; 道 dào is also a near-sound clue for 导 dǎo.
弓 (bow) — bows and tension: 张 stretch, 引 draw, 弯 bend; 弹 is to shoot or spring, and a bullet.
单 (dān) is a loose clue for dàn/tán; compare 禅 chán and 蝉 chán.

example.hanzi: 这个国家最近测试了一种新型导弹。
example.pinyin: zhège guójiā zuìjìn cèshìle yī zhǒng xīnxíng dǎodàn.
example.english: This country recently tested a new type of guided missile.
example.fact: The German V-2, first launched operationally in 1944, was the world's first long-range guided ballistic missile, reaching an altitude of about 80 kilometers — effectively becoming the first man-made object to cross into space. Its lead engineer, Wernher von Braun, later became a key figure in the American Apollo program that put astronauts on the Moon.

examples.hanzi: 新闻里说他们发射了一枚导弹。
examples.pinyin: Xīnwén lǐ shuō tāmen fāshè le yì méi dǎodàn.
examples.english: The news said they launched a missile.

examples.hanzi: 军事博物馆里展出了各种导弹的模型。
examples.pinyin: Jūnshì bówùguǎn lǐ zhǎnchū le gè zhǒng dǎodàn de móxíng.
examples.english: The military museum displays models of various missiles.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.

example.hanzi: 站在山顶俯瞰云海,那种壮观景象无比震撼。
example.pinyin: zhàn zài shāndǐng fǔkàn yúnhǎi, nà zhǒng zhuàngguān jǐngxiàng wúbǐ zhènhàn.
example.english: Standing on the mountaintop looking down at the sea of clouds, the spectacular view was incomparably stunning.
example.fact: The "sea of clouds" seen from mountain peaks like Mount Emei in China forms when moist air is trapped below a temperature inversion layer, condensing into a flat cloud deck that fills the valleys while the peaks stay clear above it. Meteorologists call this a subsidence inversion, and it is most common during calm, high-pressure weather.

examples.hanzi: 听到这个好消息，我们心情无比激动。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège hǎo xiāoxi, wǒmen xīnqíng wúbǐ jīdòng.
examples.english: Hearing the good news, we were extremely excited.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈做的饭菜美味无比。
examples.pinyin: Māma zuò de fàncài měiwèi wúbǐ.
examples.english: The food Mom makes is incomparably delicious.

meanings: a period of time in the recent past
(indicating a period of time up to the present) all along

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
向 (toward) — a window 口 in a wall facing a direction, hence toward. It also gives its sound to 响 xiǎng and 饷 xiǎng.

example.hanzi: 他一向对朋友很讲信用。
example.pinyin: tā yīxiàng duì péngyou hěn jiǎng xìnyòng.
example.english: He has always been trustworthy with his friends.
example.fact: Trust between strangers underpins the entire diamond trade in cities like Antwerp, where deals worth millions of dollars are still sealed with a handshake and the Yiddish phrase "mazal und broche" (luck and blessing) rather than a written contract. The system relies on tight-knit merchant networks where a single broken promise can permanently blacklist a trader from the community.

examples.hanzi: 我一向不喜欢吃辣的东西。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yíxiàng bù xǐhuan chī là de dōngxi.
examples.english: I have never liked spicy food.

examples.hanzi: 她做事一向很认真。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòshì yíxiàng hěn rènzhēn.
examples.english: She has always been very serious about her work.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
立 (stand) — a person standing on the ground line. As a radical it appears in 站 stand, 位 seat, 竟; also in 建立 establish.

example.hanzi: 这家公司于1998年正式成立。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī yú yījiǔjiǔbā nián zhèngshì chénglì.
example.english: This company was officially established in 1998.
example.fact: Google was legally established as a company on September 4, 1998, in a garage in Menlo Park, California, rented from Susan Wojcicki, who later became CEO of YouTube. The garage was preserved and is now marked with a small plaque commemorating it as the search engine's first office.

examples.hanzi: 学校新成立了一个足球俱乐部。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào xīn chénglì le yí gè zúqiú jùlèbù.
examples.english: The school has newly set up a football club.

examples.hanzi: 你的说法在逻辑上不成立。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shuōfǎ zài luójí shàng bù chénglì.
examples.english: Your argument doesn't hold up logically.

components.note: 甘 (sweet) — marks sweetness, as in 甘 itself and 某; 甜 pairs it with 舌 tongue: sweet to the tongue.
舌 (tongue) — the organ that tastes, as in 话 and 活.
虫 (insect) — marks insects, as in 蜂 bee, 蚊 mosquito, 蜘 spider; 蜜 is what bees make: honey.
宓 (mì) gives the sound exactly: 蜜 mì, also in 密 mì.

example.hanzi: 他们度过了一段甜蜜的蜜月旅行。
example.pinyin: tāmen dùguòle yī duàn tiánmì de mìyuè lǚxíng.
example.english: They spent a sweet honeymoon trip together.
example.fact: Bees keep their hive within about one degree of 35°C year-round by clustering and vibrating their wing muscles in winter or fanning and spreading water droplets in summer, a feat of collective thermoregulation that helps honey — which never spoils under proper storage — stay edible even centuries later, as shown by jars found in ancient Egyptian tombs.

examples.hanzi: 她脸上露出了甜蜜的笑容。
examples.pinyin: Tā liǎn shàng lùchū le tiánmì de xiàoróng.
examples.english: A sweet smile appeared on her face.

examples.hanzi: 这对新人的生活很甜蜜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duì xīnrén de shēnghuó hěn tiánmì.
examples.english: The newlyweds' life is very happy.

components.note: 里 (village, land) — in 野 it means land: open country beyond the village, wild, as in 野兽.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 野 yě is close to 预 yù and 序 xù.
兽 (simplified 獸) — the old form paired a hunted animal with a dog 犬; it means beast, as in 野兽 and 怪兽.

example.hanzi: 森林深处传来野兽的吼叫声。
example.pinyin: sēnlín shēnchù chuánlái yěshòu de hǒujiào shēng.
example.english: The roar of a wild beast came from deep in the forest.
example.fact: The Siberian tiger, the largest wild cat species alive, can weigh over 300 kilograms and once ranged across a vast swath of the Russian Far East, Korea, and northeast China. Intensive conservation since the 1940s, when fewer than 40 remained, has brought the wild population back to several hundred individuals today.

examples.hanzi: 晚上不要一个人进山，那里有野兽。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang búyào yí gè rén jìn shān, nàlǐ yǒu yěshòu.
examples.english: Don't go into the mountains alone at night; there are wild animals.

examples.hanzi: 在童话里，美女爱上了野兽。
examples.pinyin: Zài tónghuà lǐ, měinǚ àishàng le yěshòu.
examples.english: In the fairy tale, the beauty falls in love with the beast.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 移 first meant grain swaying, then shifting and moving.
多 (duō) — the original sound clue — today 移 yí is only loosely related to 多 duō.
木 (tree) — marks trees and plants, as in 树, 林, 村; 植 is to plant.
直 (zhí) gives the sound exactly: 植 zhí, also in 值 zhí and 殖 zhí.

example.hanzi: 医生成功完成了这次心脏移植手术。
example.pinyin: yīshēng chénggōng wánchéngle zhè cì xīnzàng yízhí shǒushù.
example.english: The doctors successfully completed this heart transplant surgery.
example.fact: The first successful human heart transplant was performed in 1967 by South African surgeon Christiaan Barnard, whose patient, Louis Washkansky, survived eighteen days before dying of pneumonia caused by the immunosuppressive drugs. Modern heart transplant recipients now often live well over a decade thanks to better anti-rejection medications developed in the 1980s.

examples.hanzi: 春天可以把小树苗移植到院子里。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān kěyǐ bǎ xiǎo shùmiáo yízhí dào yuànzi lǐ.
examples.english: In spring you can transplant the saplings into the yard.

examples.hanzi: 他等了很久才等到合适的肾脏移植。
examples.pinyin: Tā děng le hěn jiǔ cái děngdào héshì de shènzàng yízhí.
examples.english: He waited a long time for a suitable kidney transplant.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的本事取材于一段真实的历史事件。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng de běnshì qǔcái yú yī duàn zhēnshí de lìshǐ shìjiàn.
example.english: This film's source material is drawn from a real historical event.
example.fact: The 1975 film Jaws was based on Peter Benchley's novel of the same name, which itself was partly inspired by a series of real shark attacks along the New Jersey shore in 1916 that killed four people in twelve days. Benchley later expressed regret over the film's role in fueling shark hysteria and spent much of his later life advocating for shark conservation.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章的本事来自一个民间传说。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng de běnshì láizì yí gè mínjiān chuánshuō.
examples.english: The source story of this article comes from a folk legend.

examples.hanzi: 老师请大家先读一读故事的本事。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī qǐng dàjiā xiān dú yi dú gùshi de běnshì.
examples.english: The teacher asked everyone to first read the original story.

meanings: (sports) to break through the opponent's defense

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — the radical of holes and hollow spaces, as in 空 empty, 窗 window, 穿 pierce.
犬 (dog) — a dog bursting out of its den 穴: the picture of something sudden and unexpected.
石 (stone) — stones and hard things: 研, 码, 砖; 破 is to smash or break.
皮 (pí) is a loose sound clue; same series 坡 pō, 披 pī, 波 bō.

example.hanzi: 科学家在癌症治疗方面取得了重大突破。
example.pinyin: kēxuéjiā zài áizhèng zhìliáo fāngmiàn qǔdéle zhòngdà tūpò.
example.english: Scientists have made a major breakthrough in cancer treatment.
example.fact: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, adapted from a bacterial immune defense mechanism first noticed in yogurt cultures, lets scientists cut and edit DNA at precise locations far more cheaply and quickly than older methods. Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing the technique, only eight years after their key paper was published.

examples.hanzi: 他在比赛中突破了防线，进了一个球。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng tūpò le fángxiàn, jìn le yí gè qiú.
examples.english: He broke through the defense in the game and scored a goal.

examples.hanzi: 这位运动员的成绩突破了世界纪录。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yùndòngyuán de chéngjì tūpò le shìjiè jìlù.
examples.english: This athlete's result broke the world record.

meanings: Manhattan borough of New York City

components.note: 曼 (màn) — long, graceful; as a part it sounds out 慢 màn, 漫 màn, 馒 mán and 蔓 màn.
口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 哈 is the sound of laughing.
合 (hé) — near sound — 哈 is hā; 合 also sounds out 盒 hé.
页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 领; 顿 is to bow the head and then pause.
屯 (tún) — near sound — 顿 is dùn; 屯 also sounds out 钝 dùn and 炖 dùn.

example.hanzi: 自由女神像就在曼哈顿附近的一个小岛上。
example.pinyin: zìyóu nǚshén xiàng jiù zài Mànhādùn fùjìn de yī gè xiǎo dǎo shàng.
example.english: The Statue of Liberty stands on a small island near Manhattan.
example.fact: Manhattan was purchased by the Dutch West India Company from the local Lenape people in 1626, according to a letter describing the deal as worth 60 guilders — a figure later popularized as "$24," though the actual value and fairness of the exchange are disputed, since the Lenape likely understood it as a temporary land-use agreement rather than an outright sale.

examples.hanzi: 曼哈顿的房租贵得吓人。
examples.pinyin: Mànhādùn de fángzū guì de xiàrén.
examples.english: Rent in Manhattan is shockingly expensive.

examples.hanzi: 我们在曼哈顿的一家小餐馆吃了晚饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài Mànhādùn de yì jiā xiǎo cānguǎn chī le wǎnfàn.
examples.english: We had dinner at a small restaurant in Manhattan.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — marks bows and bending, as in 弯, 引, 张, 强; 弱 doubles the shape and pairs with 强 strong.

example.hanzi: 他的身体很弱。
example.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ hěn ruò.
example.english: His health is weak.
example.fact: 弱 is the opposite of 强: 软弱 (weak), 弱点 (weakness), 弱者 (the weak). After a fraction it means 'a little less than', as in 三分之一弱 (just under one-third).

examples.hanzi: 这个队的实力比较弱。
examples.pinyin: Zhège duì de shílì bǐjiào ruò.
examples.english: This team's strength is relatively weak.

examples.hanzi: 网络信号太弱了,打不开页面。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngluò xìnhào tài ruò le, dǎ bu kāi yèmiàn.
examples.english: The network signal is too weak to open the page.

components.note: 方 (fāng) hints at the sound: 妨 fáng is close to 防 fáng and 房 fáng, which share it.
石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破 break, 码, 砖 brick; a stone in the road is an obstacle.

example.hanzi: 噪音妨碍了他们正常的睡眠。
example.pinyin: zàoyīn fáng'àile tāmen zhèngcháng de shuìmián.
example.english: The noise interfered with their normal sleep.
example.fact: Chronic exposure to nighttime noise above about 40 decibels — roughly the level of a quiet refrigerator hum — has been linked by the World Health Organization to measurable increases in cardiovascular disease risk, because the body's stress hormone levels can rise even during sleep stages when a person never consciously wakes up.

examples.hanzi: 请不要把东西放在走廊，会妨碍别人通行。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng búyào bǎ dōngxi fàng zài zǒuláng, huì fáng'ài biéren tōngxíng.
examples.english: Please don't leave things in the hallway; they will obstruct others.

examples.hanzi: 我这样说，不会妨碍你的工作吧？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhèyàng shuō, bú huì fáng'ài nǐ de gōngzuò ba?
examples.english: I hope talking like this isn't getting in the way of your work.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talk: 说, 论, 请; 评 is to comment and judge.
平 (píng) sounds exactly like 评; also in 苹 píng.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; 审 is a hearing held in a hall.
申 (shēn) is a near sound match for shěn; also in 神 shén, 伸 shēn.

example.hanzi: 评审委员会将从三十份作品中选出获奖者。
example.pinyin: píngshěn wěiyuánhuì jiāng cóng sānshí fèn zuòpǐn zhōng xuǎnchū huòjiǎngzhě.
example.english: The judging panel will select the winner from thirty entries.
example.fact: The Nobel Prize committees keep their nomination records sealed for fifty years, so historians only learned in the 2010s that Mahatma Gandhi had been nominated for the Peace Prize five times between 1937 and 1948 but never won — a gap the Nobel Foundation has publicly called one of its most significant omissions.

examples.hanzi: 评审老师给她的作品打了很高的分。
examples.pinyin: Píngshěn lǎoshī gěi tā de zuòpǐn dǎ le hěn gāo de fēn.
examples.english: The judging teachers gave her work a high score.

examples.hanzi: 项目需要经过专家评审才能通过。
examples.pinyin: Xiàngmù xūyào jīngguò zhuānjiā píngshěn cáinéng tōngguò.
examples.english: The project must be evaluated by experts before it can be approved.

components.note: 友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他向自己的爱人许下了永远的承诺。
example.pinyin: tā xiàng zìjǐ de àiren xǔxiàle yǒngyuǎn de chéngnuò.
example.english: He made an eternal promise to his beloved.
example.fact: The Taj Mahal in Agra, India, was commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in 1632 as a mausoleum for his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal, who died giving birth to their fourteenth child. It took roughly 20,000 workers and over a decade to complete, and its white marble is said to shift color from pink at dawn to golden under moonlight.

examples.hanzi: 我爱人今天出差，晚上不回家吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ àiren jīntiān chūchāi, wǎnshang bù huí jiā chīfàn.
examples.english: My spouse is on a business trip today and won't be home for dinner.

examples.hanzi: 他和爱人结婚已经二十年了。
examples.pinyin: Tā hé àiren jiéhūn yǐjīng èrshí nián le.
examples.english: He and his wife have been married for twenty years.

components.note: 尸 (body) — a body with 毛 fur behind it is a tail; 尸 also in 屁, 尿 and 层.
毛 (hair, fur) — the furry tip hanging off the back.

example.hanzi: 小狗摇着尾巴跑过来。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu yáo zhe wěiba pǎo guòlái.
example.english: The puppy ran over wagging its tail.
example.fact: 尾 is a tail or the end of something: 尾巴 (tail), 结尾 (ending), 年尾 (year-end). It is also a measure word for fish in formal writing: 一尾鱼 'a fish'.

examples.hanzi: 请排在队伍的最后,站到队尾去。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng pái zài duìwǔ de zuìhòu, zhàn dào duìwěi qù.
examples.english: Please go to the end of the line.

examples.hanzi: 这条鱼的尾巴很长。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo yú de wěiba hěn cháng.
examples.english: This fish has a long tail.

components.note: 手 (hand) — marks hand actions, as in 拿, 打; 摩 is to rub with the hand.
麻 (má) gives the sound: 摩 mó is close, as in 魔 mó and 磨 mó.

example.hanzi: 冬天他常常摩擦双手取暖。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān tā chángcháng mócā shuāngshǒu qǔnuǎn.
example.english: In winter he often rubs his hands to keep warm.
example.fact: 摩 means 'to rub', as in 摩擦 (friction), 按摩 (massage) and 摩托车 (motorcycle, from 'motor'). 摩天大楼 is a skyscraper, a building that 'rubs the sky'.

examples.hanzi: 他在给爷爷按摩肩膀。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gěi yéye ànmó jiānbǎng.
examples.english: He is massaging Grandpa's shoulders.

examples.hanzi: 我们坐摩天轮看夜景。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò mótiānlún kàn yèjǐng.
examples.english: We ride the Ferris wheel to see the night view.

components.note: 未 (not yet) — a tree 木 with a new short branch on top, still growing. Compare 末 mò (end/tip), where the top stroke is longer.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐; oldest form shows a hand arranging a woman's hair, a wife.

example.hanzi: 他终于向未婚妻求婚,并订下了婚期。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú xiàng wèihūnqī qiúhūn, bìng dìngxiàle hūnqī.
example.english: He finally proposed to his fiancée and set a wedding date.
example.fact: The diamond engagement ring tradition traces largely to a 1938 De Beers advertising campaign built around the slogan "A Diamond Is Forever," which successfully reframed a once-optional gift into a near-universal social expectation across much of the English-speaking world within about two decades.

examples.hanzi: 他带着未婚妻回家见父母。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàizhe wèihūnqī huí jiā jiàn fùmǔ.
examples.english: He took his fiancée home to meet his parents.

examples.hanzi: 她的未婚妻是一位医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā de wèihūnqī shì yí wèi yīshēng.
examples.english: His fiancée is a doctor.

components.note: 又 (hand) — 双 (simplified 雙) shows two birds held in one hand: a pair; the simplified form just doubles the hand 又又.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 她双手捧着那本珍贵的古书。
example.pinyin: tā shuāngshǒu pěngzhe nà běn zhēnguì de gǔshū.
example.english: She held the precious old book with both hands.
example.fact: The human hand contains 27 bones — 8 in the wrist, 5 in the palm, and 14 in the fingers — making up roughly a quarter of all the bones in the entire body, which is part of why hand surgery is considered one of the most technically demanding specialties in orthopedics.

examples.hanzi: 进门前请先洗双手。
examples.pinyin: Jìnmén qián qǐng xiān xǐ shuāngshǒu.
examples.english: Please wash both hands before coming in.

examples.hanzi: 他用双手接过了那份礼物。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng shuāngshǒu jiēguò le nà fèn lǐwù.
examples.english: He received the gift with both hands.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
廾 (two hands) — two hands joined — 共 is doing together; it also sounds out 供 gōng.

example.hanzi: 这次旅行一共花了我们五千块钱。
example.pinyin: zhè cì lǚxíng yīgòng huāle wǒmen wǔqiān kuài qián.
example.english: This trip cost us five thousand yuan in total.
example.fact: The Grand Tour, a rite of passage for wealthy young Europeans from roughly the 1660s to the 1840s, could take a traveler through Italy, France, and Switzerland for a year or more and cost a small fortune in total — the eighteenth-century equivalent of hundreds of thousands of dollars once servants, carriages, and souvenirs were counted.

examples.hanzi: 这些东西一共多少钱？
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōngxi yígòng duōshao qián?
examples.english: How much is all of this in total?

examples.hanzi: 我们班一共有三十个学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān yígòng yǒu sānshí gè xuésheng.
examples.english: There are thirty students in our class altogether.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water and liquids, as in 海, 汤, 酒; 液 is a liquid.
夜 (yè) — same sound — 液 is yè, like 夜 night.

example.hanzi: 这瓶液体有一股酸味。
example.pinyin: Zhè píng yètǐ yǒu yì gǔ suānwèi.
example.english: This bottle of liquid has a sour smell.
example.fact: 液 is a bound word for liquid: 液体 (liquid), 血液 (blood), 溶液 (solution) and 洗手液 (hand sanitizer). It is more scientific than 水, which is the everyday word.

examples.hanzi: 请把这瓶溶液摇一摇。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè píng róngyè yáo yi yáo.
examples.english: Please shake this bottle of solution.

examples.hanzi: 她对血液检查很紧张。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì xuèyè jiǎnchá hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: She is nervous about the blood test.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 挥 is to wave or wield.
军 (jūn) — near sound — 挥 is huī; 军 also sounds out 辉 huī.

example.hanzi: 他向我们挥手告别。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàng wǒmen huīshǒu gàobié.
example.english: He waved goodbye to us.
example.fact: 挥 means to wave or swing: 挥手 (wave a hand), 挥舞 (brandish). It also builds 发挥 (bring into play), 指挥 (to command, conduct) and 挥霍 (to squander money).

examples.hanzi: 他挥动着手里的小旗子。
examples.pinyin: Tā huīdòng zhe shǒu li de xiǎo qízi.
examples.english: He is waving the little flag in his hand.

examples.hanzi: 教练在场边指挥队员。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoliàn zài chǎng biān zhǐhuī duìyuán.
examples.english: The coach is directing the players from the sideline.

components.note: 巫 — shaman: a ritual tool 工 with two figures 人 dancing on either side. 巫 wū also sounds out 诬 wū.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 传说中的巫师能用咒语召唤风雨。
example.pinyin: chuánshuō zhōng de wūshī néng yòng zhòuyǔ zhàohuàn fēngyǔ.
example.english: The legendary wizard could summon wind and rain with incantations.
example.fact: Archaeological evidence for shaman-like ritual specialists goes back at least 12,000 years — a grave in northern Israel known as the "Shaman of Hilazon Tachtit" held the remains of an elderly woman buried with tortoise shells, a human foot, and eagle wing bones, interpreted by archaeologists as a shamanic burial.

examples.hanzi: 哈利·波特是一个年轻的巫师。
examples.pinyin: Hālì Bōtè shì yí gè niánqīng de wūshī.
examples.english: Harry Potter is a young wizard.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的巫师给王子施了魔法。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de wūshī gěi wángzǐ shī le mófǎ.
examples.english: The wizard in the story cast a spell on the prince.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 石 as in 破 break, 砖 brick: hard things colliding — 碰 is to bump into.
並 (bìng) — loose hint — 碰 is pèng; 並 (bìng) also sounds out 拼 pīn and 屏 píng.
工 (work, craft) — craft and skill — clever handiwork; also in 左, 差.
丂 (kǎo) — near sound — 巧 qiǎo; 丂 also sounds out 考 kǎo and 烤 kǎo.

example.hanzi: 我碰巧在机场遇到了多年不见的老同学。
example.pinyin: wǒ pèngqiǎo zài jīchǎng yù dàole duōnián bùjiàn de lǎo tóngxué.
example.english: I happened to run into an old classmate I hadn't seen in years at the airport.
example.fact: Penicillin was discovered by chance in 1928 when Alexander Fleming returned from vacation to find that mold had contaminated a petri dish of bacteria he had left out, and noticed the bacteria near the mold had died. That accidental observation eventually led to the first mass-produced antibiotic, saving an estimated hundreds of millions of lives since.

examples.hanzi: 我去商店的时候，碰巧遇到了老师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù shāngdiàn de shíhou, pèngqiǎo yùdào le lǎoshī.
examples.english: When I went to the store, I happened to run into my teacher.

examples.hanzi: 你来得真碰巧，我刚做好饭。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lái de zhēn pèngqiǎo, wǒ gāng zuò hǎo fàn.
examples.english: You came at just the right time; I've just finished cooking.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
令 (order) — a person kneeling under a command from above. Its sound spreads to 冷 lěng, 零 líng, 铃 líng, 领 lǐng and 怜 lián.

example.hanzi: 计算机严格按照程序员给出的指令执行任务。
example.pinyin: jìsuànjī yángé ànzhào chéngxùyuán gěichū de zhǐlìng zhíxíng rènwù.
example.english: The computer strictly executes tasks according to the instructions given by the programmer.
example.fact: The Apollo Guidance Computer that navigated astronauts to the Moon in 1969 had roughly 4 kilobytes of RAM and ran at just over 1 megahertz, millions of times slower than a modern smartphone — yet its carefully written assembly-language instruction sets were robust enough to recover from a nearly catastrophic 1202 alarm during the Apollo 11 landing itself.

examples.hanzi: 士兵必须服从上级的指令。
examples.pinyin: Shìbīng bìxū fúcóng shàngjí de zhǐlìng.
examples.english: Soldiers must obey orders from their superiors.

examples.hanzi: 输入这条指令后，电脑就会自动重启。
examples.pinyin: Shūrù zhè tiáo zhǐlìng hòu, diànnǎo jiù huì zìdòng chóngqǐ.
examples.english: After entering this command, the computer will restart automatically.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord words: 红 red, 给 give, 线 line; a thread has an end, which fits 终 end.
冬 (dōng) rhymes with 终 zhōng, and 冬 originally meant the end (of the year) too — so it helps sound and sense.

example.hanzi: 我们终于到家了。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngyú dào jiā le.
example.english: We've finally arrived home.
example.fact: 终 is the 'end' in 终于 (finally, implying a long wait), 终点 (terminus) and 最终 (ultimate). 终身 means 'lifelong' and 始终 means 'from start to finish'.

examples.hanzi: 终于放假了!
examples.pinyin: Zhōngyú fàngjià le!
examples.english: Finally, it's vacation!

examples.hanzi: 他们的比赛最终以平局结束。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de bǐsài zuìzhōng yǐ píngjú jiéshù.
examples.english: Their match ended in a draw.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.
巾 (cloth) — marks cloth and coverings, as in 布, 帽, 带; decorating was often done with cloth.
饣 (here from 食 shí) is the sound part: 饰 shì is close.

example.hanzi: 圣诞树上挂满了五颜六色的装饰品。
example.pinyin: shèngdàn shù shàng guàmǎnle wǔyánliùsè de zhuāngshì pǐn.
example.english: The Christmas tree was covered in colorful decorations.
example.fact: The tradition of decorating evergreen trees indoors is often traced to 16th-century Germany, where guild records from Freiburg describe a decorated tree as early as 1419, adorned with apples, nuts, and paper flowers long before electric lights existed — those came only after Edward Johnson, a colleague of Thomas Edison, strung the first electrically lit Christmas tree in New York in 1882.

examples.hanzi: 我们用气球装饰了教室。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yòng qìqiú zhuāngshì le jiàoshì.
examples.english: We decorated the classroom with balloons.

examples.hanzi: 这面墙上的装饰很有特色。
examples.pinyin: Zhè miàn qiáng shàng de zhuāngshì hěn yǒu tèsè.
examples.english: The decoration on this wall is very distinctive.

components.note: 石 (stone) — a rock 口 at the foot of a cliff 厂; as a radical it marks stones and minerals, as in 破, 码, 砖, 磨.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — marks liquids and things that flow, as in 河 river, 汤 soup, 酒 liquor; here an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) sounds exactly like 油 — the same sound clue appears in 邮 yóu and 柚 yòu.

example.hanzi: 中东地区拥有全球最丰富的石油储量。
example.pinyin: zhōngdōng dìqū yōngyǒu quánqiú zuì fēngfù de shíyóu chǔliàng.
example.english: The Middle East holds the world's richest petroleum reserves.
example.fact: The 1859 Drake Well in Titusville, Pennsylvania, drilled to just 21 meters deep, is widely credited as the first commercial oil well in the United States, kicking off an oil boom that within a decade turned a small farming town into a hub of speculation, refineries, and, eventually, John D. Rockefeller's Standard Oil empire.

examples.hanzi: 石油价格上涨，汽油也变贵了。
examples.pinyin: Shíyóu jiàgé shàngzhǎng, qìyóu yě biàn guì le.
examples.english: Oil prices rose and gasoline got more expensive too.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家的经济主要靠出口石油。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de jīngjì zhǔyào kào chūkǒu shíyóu.
examples.english: This country's economy mainly depends on exporting oil.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 伦 is about human relations and order, 伦理 ethics.
仑 (lún) — same sound — 仑 also sounds out 轮 lún and 论 lùn.

example.hanzi: 这是一个很有意思的伦理问题。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè hěn yǒu yìsi de lúnlǐ wèntí.
example.english: This is a very interesting ethical question.
example.fact: 伦 is a bound word about human order: 伦理 (ethics), 人伦 (human relationships). It is also used in transliterations like 伦敦 (London), and 无与伦比 means 'peerless'.

examples.hanzi: 他在伦敦留学。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài Lúndūn liúxué.
examples.english: He is studying in London.

examples.hanzi: 我们不能违反社会伦理。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù néng wéifǎn shèhuì lúnlǐ.
examples.english: We must not violate social ethics.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
釆 (distinguish) — sorting things out: 释 is to untangle and explain.
圣 stands in for 睪 in the traditional 釋; the same part is in 译 yì, 泽 zé and 择 zé.

example.hanzi: 被告缴纳了十万元保释金后获释。
example.pinyin: bèigào jiǎonàle shíwàn yuán bǎoshì jīn hòu huòshì.
example.english: The defendant was released after paying a bail of one hundred thousand yuan.
example.fact: The concept of bail dates back at least to the Statute of Westminster in 1275 in England, which formally distinguished which offenses were bailable and which were not, aiming to prevent sheriffs from arbitrarily jailing suspects indefinitely — a principle that later shaped the Eighth Amendment's protection against excessive bail in the U.S. Constitution.

examples.hanzi: 律师为他申请了保释。
examples.pinyin: Lǜshī wèi tā shēnqǐng le bǎoshì.
examples.english: The lawyer applied for bail for him.

examples.hanzi: 法官同意保释，但要求他不能离开本市。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān tóngyì bǎoshì, dàn yāoqiú tā bù néng líkāi běn shì.
examples.english: The judge agreed to bail but required that he not leave the city.

components.note: 写 (xiě) — to write; as a part it sounds out 泻 xiè (to flow out).
亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.

example.hanzi: 奶奶还是喜欢用手写信给远方的亲人。
example.pinyin: nǎinai háishi xǐhuan yòng shǒu xiěxìn gěi yuǎnfāng de qīnrén.
example.english: Grandma still likes to write letters by hand to family far away.
example.fact: During World War II, British and American postal services used a technique called V-mail (Victory Mail), photographically reducing handwritten letters onto microfilm to save enormous cargo space on military transport — a single reel of film could carry the equivalent of over 1,500 kilograms of paper letters.

examples.hanzi: 现在很少有人给朋友写信了。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài hěn shǎo yǒu rén gěi péngyou xiěxìn le.
examples.english: Few people write letters to friends now.

examples.hanzi: 我想给老师写信，感谢她的帮助。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gěi lǎoshī xiěxìn, gǎnxiè tā de bāngzhù.
examples.english: I want to write a letter to my teacher to thank her for her help.

components.note: 舌 — a picture of a tongue sticking out of a mouth; compare 活 and 话 which use it as a part.

example.hanzi: 他吐了吐舌头。
example.pinyin: Tā tǔ le tǔ shétou.
example.english: He stuck out his tongue.
example.fact: 舌 is the tongue, usually 舌头 in speech, and it is a part of 舌尖 (tip of the tongue). The documentary 舌尖上的中国 (A Bite of China) is named for this idea. 口舌 can mean 'quarrelling' too.

examples.hanzi: 他舌头烫伤了。
examples.pinyin: Tā shétou tàngshāng le.
examples.english: He burned his tongue.

examples.hanzi: 这杯汤太咸,我的舌尖都麻了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi tāng tài xián, wǒ de shéjiān dōu má le.
examples.english: This soup is so salty my tongue tip is numb.

components.note: 月 (moon) — moonlight, clear and bright; also in 明 bright.
良 (liáng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 浪 làng, 狼 láng and 郎 láng.

example.hanzi: 今天天气晴朗。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì qínglǎng.
example.english: The weather is clear and bright today.
example.fact: 朗 appears in 晴朗 (clear sky), 开朗 (cheerful, outgoing) and in the loud-reading words 朗读 and 朗诵. 朗朗 describes a clear voice, as in 朗朗上口 'easy to read aloud'.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在大声朗读课文。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài dàshēng lǎngdú kèwén.
examples.english: The children are reading the text aloud.

examples.hanzi: 他的性格很开朗。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xìnggé hěn kāilǎng.
examples.english: He has a cheerful personality.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and questions, as in 说, 请, 问; 诊 is a doctor questioning and examining.
㐱 (zhěn) gives the sound exactly: 诊 zhěn, also in 疹 zhěn.
斤 (axe) — 斤 is an axe, as in 新, 析; 断 is to cut through, shown by the axe and threads cut.

example.hanzi: 医生根据检查结果做出了准确的诊断。
example.pinyin: yīshēng gēnjù jiǎnchá jiéguǒ zuòchūle zhǔnquè de zhěnduàn.
example.english: The doctor made an accurate diagnosis based on the test results.
example.fact: Stethoscopes were invented in 1816 by French physician René Laennec, who reportedly rolled a sheet of paper into a tube to listen to a patient's heart without pressing his ear directly against her chest, a practice considered improper at the time — his simple wooden tube design remained largely unchanged in principle for over a century.

examples.hanzi: 医生诊断他得了重感冒。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng zhěnduàn tā dé le zhòng gǎnmào.
examples.english: The doctor diagnosed him with a bad cold.

examples.hanzi: 这个诊断需要进一步检查来确认。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhěnduàn xūyào jìnyíbù jiǎnchá lái quèrèn.
examples.english: This diagnosis needs further tests to confirm.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 撤 is to pull away. The right side matches old 徹 (now 彻 chè), which gave the sound.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 退 is to step back.

example.hanzi: 军队在深夜悄悄撤退到山后。
example.pinyin: jūnduì zài shēnyè qiāoqiāo chètuì dào shān hòu.
example.english: The army quietly retreated behind the mountain in the dead of night.
example.fact: The Dunkirk evacuation of 1940 rescued over 330,000 Allied soldiers from the beaches of northern France in just nine days, using a mix of Royal Navy destroyers and hundreds of civilian fishing boats and pleasure craft — an operation originally expected by British commanders to save only about 45,000 troops.

examples.hanzi: 雨越下越大，登山队决定撤退。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ yuè xià yuè dà, dēngshānduì juédìng chètuì.
examples.english: The rain grew heavier, and the climbing team decided to retreat.

examples.hanzi: 面对强大的对手，他们只好撤退。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì qiángdà de duìshǒu, tāmen zhǐhǎo chètuì.
examples.english: Facing a strong opponent, they had no choice but to pull back.

components.note: 女 (woman) — marks women, as in 妈, 姐, 好; 姓 first meant the clan traced through mothers.
生 (shēng) hints at the sound: 姓 xìng is close to 性 xìng and 星 xīng, which share it.
口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.hanzi: 请在表格上填写你的姓名和出生日期。
example.pinyin: qǐng zài biǎogé shàng tiánxiě nǐ de xìngmíng hé chūshēng rìqī.
example.english: Please fill in your full name and date of birth on the form.
example.fact: Iceland's naming system still largely follows the old Norse patronymic tradition, so most Icelanders have no inherited surname at all — a person's "last name" is typically their father's or mother's first name plus "-son" or "-dóttir," which is why the country's phone directory is alphabetized by first name.

examples.hanzi: 请在这里写上您的姓名和电话。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ xiě shàng nín de xìngmíng hé diànhuà.
examples.english: Please write your name and phone number here.

examples.hanzi: 老师点了每个同学的姓名。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī diǎn le měi gè tóngxué de xìngmíng.
examples.english: The teacher called out each student's name.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and relatives: 妈, 姐, 姑; 奶 is milk or a grandmother.
乃 (nǎi) sounds exactly like 奶.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — marks liquids and things that flow, as in 河 river, 汤 soup, 酒 liquor; here an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) sounds exactly like 油 — the same sound clue appears in 邮 yóu and 柚 yòu.

example.hanzi: 蛋糕上挤满了雪白的奶油。
example.pinyin: dàngāo shàng jǐmǎnle xuěbái de nǎiyóu.
example.english: The cake was piled high with snow-white cream.
example.fact: Butter churning was independently discovered across many ancient pastoral cultures, and Tibetan butter tea, made by churning yak butter, salt, and tea together, has been a staple at high altitude for over a thousand years because the fat provides quick, dense calories in an environment where crops barely grow.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢在咖啡里加一点奶油。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài kāfēi lǐ jiā yìdiǎn nǎiyóu.
examples.english: I like adding a little cream to my coffee.

examples.hanzi: 这个奶油蛋糕太甜了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège nǎiyóu dàngāo tài tián le.
examples.english: This cream cake is too sweet.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海; 沿 is to go along a stream's edge, hence to follow.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 我们沿着河边散步,欣赏两岸的风景。
example.pinyin: wǒmen yánzhe hébiān sànbù, xīnshǎng liǎng'àn de fēngjǐng.
example.english: We walked along the riverbank, enjoying the scenery on both sides.
example.fact: The Amazon River has no bridges crossing its main channel anywhere along its nearly 6,400-kilometer length, largely because the surrounding rainforest has too few roads to justify one in the first place — most crossings are made by ferry.

examples.hanzi: 沿着这条路一直走，就能看到车站。
examples.pinyin: Yánzhe zhè tiáo lù yìzhí zǒu, jiù néng kàndào chēzhàn.
examples.english: Walk straight along this road and you'll see the station.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们沿着小溪跑来跑去。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen yánzhe xiǎoxī pǎolái pǎoqù.
examples.english: The children ran back and forth along the stream.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
父 (father) — 父 marks older male relatives, as in 爸 dad; 爷 is grandfather.
耶 (yé) — the old form 爺 had 耶 giving the sound yé — the simplified 爷 keeps just a trace of it.

example.hanzi: 老天爷终于下雨了,农民们松了一口气。
example.pinyin: lǎotiānyé zhōngyú xiàyǔle, nóngmínmen sōngle yī kǒu qì.
example.english: Heavens, it finally rained, and the farmers breathed a sigh of relief.
example.fact: Rainmaking rituals appear across nearly every ancient agricultural civilization, from Hopi rain dances in the American Southwest to Chinese dragon-worship ceremonies for rain during drought — a reflection of how directly early societies' survival depended on rainfall timing that they had no scientific way to predict or control.

examples.hanzi: 老天爷，这怎么可能！
examples.pinyin: Lǎotiānyé, zhè zěnme kěnéng!
examples.english: Heavens, how could this be possible!

examples.hanzi: 他求老天爷保佑全家人平安。
examples.pinyin: Tā qiú lǎotiānyé bǎoyòu quánjiā rén píng'ān.
examples.english: He prayed to Heaven to keep his whole family safe.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 marks feelings, as in 想, 爱, 怒; 悲 is sorrow.
非 (fēi) — near sound — 悲 is bēi; 非 also sounds out 辈 bèi and 排 pái.
忄 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 情, 怕, 悲; 惨 is a wretched, painful feeling.
参 (cān) gives the sound: 惨 cǎn is close, as in 掺 chān.

example.hanzi: 战争给这个村庄带来了悲惨的命运。
example.pinyin: zhànzhēng gěi zhège cūnzhuāng dàiláile bēicǎn de mìngyùn.
example.english: The war brought a tragic fate to this village.
example.fact: The 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia was the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded history, ejecting so much ash into the atmosphere that it caused a "Year Without a Summer" in 1816, leading to crop failures, famine, and tens of thousands of deaths across Europe and North America.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事的结局非常悲惨。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi de jiéjú fēicháng bēicǎn.
examples.english: The ending of this story is very tragic.

examples.hanzi: 他小时候的生活十分悲惨。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎo shíhou de shēnghuó shífēn bēicǎn.
examples.english: His childhood was miserable.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买; 资 is capital or resources.
次 (cì) is a loose clue; same part in 姿 zī and 咨 zī.
氵 (water) — marks water and rivers, as in 河, 海; 源 is the spring where water starts.
原 (yuán) gives the sound exactly: 源 yuán, also in 愿 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 水是地球上最宝贵的自然资源之一。
example.pinyin: shuǐ shì dìqiú shàng zuì bǎoguì de zìrán zīyuán zhī yī.
example.english: Water is one of the most precious natural resources on Earth.
example.fact: Although roughly 71% of Earth's surface is covered in water, only about 0.5% of it is accessible fresh water suitable for drinking, since most is seawater or locked away in glaciers and deep groundwater — a scarcity that has made freshwater access a growing point of geopolitical tension in arid regions.

examples.hanzi: 这个学习网站有很多免费资源。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xuéxí wǎngzhàn yǒu hěn duō miǎnfèi zīyuán.
examples.english: This learning website has lots of free resources.

examples.hanzi: 我们不能浪费地球的资源。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù néng làngfèi dìqiú de zīyuán.
examples.english: We can't waste the Earth's resources.

components.note: 瓦 (tile, pottery) — marks pottery and fired clay, as in 瓷 china; 瓶 is a bottle.
并 (bìng) hints at the sound: 瓶 píng is close to 拼 pīn and 屏 píng.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他把写好的信放进瓶子,扔进了大海。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ xiěhǎo de xìn fàng jìn píngzi, rēng jìnle dàhǎi.
example.english: He put the finished letter into a bottle and threw it into the sea.
example.fact: The longest-known drifting message in a bottle was found in 2018 on a German beach 132 years after it was tossed into the sea in 1886 as part of a Marine Biological Association experiment studying ocean currents — the postcard inside was still legible enough to identify the ship that released it.

examples.hanzi: 桌子上放着一个空瓶子。
examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng fàngzhe yí gè kōng píngzi.
examples.english: There is an empty bottle on the table.

examples.hanzi: 请把用完的瓶子扔到回收桶里。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yòng wán de píngzi rēng dào huíshōutǒng lǐ.
examples.english: Please throw used bottles into the recycling bin.

components.note: 反 (opposite) — 反 means opposite or against — 叛 is going against, rebelling.
半 (bàn) — near sound — 叛 is pàn; 半 also sounds out 伴 bàn and 拌 bàn.
彳 (step) — marks walking, as in 行, 往, 很, 得; 徒 pairs it with 走 walk: going on foot, then a follower.
走 (walk) — as in 跑 run, 起 rise.

example.hanzi: 历史书上把他描述成一个可耻的叛徒。
example.pinyin: lìshǐ shū shàng bǎ tā miáoshù chéng yī gè kěchǐ de pàntú.
example.english: History books describe him as a shameful traitor.
example.fact: Benedict Arnold, once one of George Washington's most trusted generals in the American Revolutionary War, defected to the British side in 1780 after feeling passed over for promotion and facing debt — his name became so synonymous with betrayal in the United States that it is still used today as a common insult for anyone who switches sides.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的叛徒最后被抓住了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de pàntú zuìhòu bèi zhuāzhù le.
examples.english: The traitor in the movie was caught in the end.

examples.hanzi: 他不愿意被人看成叛徒。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú yuànyì bèi rén kànchéng pàntú.
examples.english: He doesn't want to be seen as a traitor.
